draft.title: Area references
card: Many maps have a grid of squares made by lines that run up and down and across. Each line has a number printed along the edge of the map.
The lines that run up and down give the easting. Eastings are read along the bottom or top edge, from left to right.
The lines that run across give the northing. Northings are read along the side edge, from bottom to top.

A four-figure area reference names a whole grid square. Give the easting first, then the northing. Use the numbers of the lines at the bottom left corner of the square. Easting 45 and northing 12 gives 4512.
draft.remember: Easting first, then northing: along the corridor, then up the stairs.

a.q: A school sits in the grid square whose bottom left corner is where easting line 27 meets northing line 63. What is its four-figure area reference?
a.why: Easting goes first, so 27 comes before 63, giving 2763. The reference 6327 is tempting, but it swaps the order and would name a different square.
a.clue: Which number do you read first, along or up?

b.q: Jack finds a lookout in the square 3158 on a map. Which describes where the lookout is?
opts: Between easting lines 31 and 32, northing lines 58 and 59
Between easting lines 58 and 59, northing lines 31 and 32
Exactly on easting line 31 and northing line 58
Between easting lines 15 and 16, northing lines 38 and 39
b.why: The first two figures are the easting, 31, and the last two are the northing, 58. The square starts at those lines, so it lies between 31 and 32 and between 58 and 59. The second option swaps the order.
b.clue: The first two figures are the easting.

b.best: Between easting lines 31 and 32, northing lines 58 and 59
